text:
sam: Hey team, noticed an automated audit export to our internal GCS bucket contained an "exported_events.csv" with some columns that look like wrapped KMS ciphertext fragments. File path: gs://redwood-exports/sandbox/audit-exports/2024-11-02/exported_events.csv
nina: @sam can you paste a single offending row (redact anything PII)?
sam: here's a redacted row (copied from CSV):
"ts","actor","resource","event","metadata"
"2024-11-02T10:12:03Z","svc-audit-exporter@redwood","projects/redwood/keys/crypto-key-id-abc","access_token_read","{\"key_wrap\":\"CiQA...base64...==\",\"key_id\":\"projects/123/locations/global/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/ck-42\"}"
jules: that key_id in metadata is the KMS resource id (not the raw key), but it still gives an attacker the key path and likely the wrapped ciphertext fragment.
andrew: how did the exporter include KMS metadata in the CSV? export pipeline should strip that.
sam: looks like our audit-formatter step marshals the entire event JSON into "metadata" column without filtering. I ran `gsutil cat` and confirmed the last 3 days of exports have similar rows.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20241102-1. Severity: medium. Triage channel: #eng-security. Owner assigned: nina.
nina: assigning myself to coordinate. First actions:
- stop new exports to that bucket
- rotate IAM creds for svc-audit-exporter
- remove existing CSV files from public access (set object ACL)
- convo with vendor if their agent is involved
kai: I can stop the export job in batch pipeline. running:
```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment audit-exporter --replicas=0
```
jules: also lock down the service account: remove roles/storage.objects.get for the audit-exporter SA and create short-lived tokens for debugging only.
andrew: we should also check Cloud Audit Logs ingestion — if any downstream vendor pulled these exports via their integration.
sam: pinging @vendor-ops now: vendor-ops, did your SaaS agent pull from gs://redwood-exports/sandbox/audit-exports/?
vendor-ops: yes we had a one-off connector subscribed to that prefix for demo ingestion last week. We pulled the CSVs on 2024-11-02 10:20Z and have them archived. We're pausing ingestion and will delete our copies on confirmation.
nina: vendor-ops: please provide an inventory of archived files and cert that you'll delete them securely. also need a signed attestation (S3/GCS delete + shredding logs) within 2 hours.
vendor-ops: will produce attestation in 90m. files list: demo-exports-2024-11-02.tar.gz (contains exported_events.csv)
andrew: action items and owners (initial):
- kai: stop exporter and block new writes to bucket — done by 10:25Z (in progress)
- nina: request vendor attestation + coordinate SLA/legal — due 12:00Z
- sam: list affected CSV objects and snapshot sample rows for forensics (sensitive fields redacted) — due 11:00Z
- jules: prepare KMS impact assessment (is key compromised?) and consult with cloud-kms team — due 12:30Z
- security-oncall (me): create short-term policy: disable key decryption for that key until assessment complete
jules: quick KMS note: wrapped ciphertext fragments in logs are not plaintext but could help fingerprint key usage or aid offline cryptanalysis if attacker has ciphertext pool; treat as sensitive.
andrew: for RBAC changes, plan is:
1) remove long-lived SA keys for svc-audit-exporter
2) create ephemeral workload identity (OIDC) for exporter with limited roles
3) add constraint that exported artifacts cannot contain metadata.key_wrap or key_id fields (pipeline filter)
sam: for immediate mitigation I created a policy to deny objectReads from all non-admin principals on that prefix and added a lifecycle rule to quarantine copies for 30d (will be gated by legal) — applied at 10:40Z.
kai: exporter scaled down at 10:26Z. no new writes after that.
vendor-ops: attestation attached (vendor-attest-1748891230.pdf) — we confirm deletion at 11:45Z and provide md5 of deleted archive.
nina: good. next: rotation options. If KMS key was used only for wrapping and not the underlying plaintext exposure, we can rewrap without changing key material. If key path is leaked and we suspect misuse, rekey (create new key version) and initiate rewrap of current ciphertext blobs.
jules: cloud-kms team advised: create a new key version (versions 2) and rotate via `gcloud kms keys versions create` then run rewrap job for any stored ciphertext we control. timeline ~4h for small dataset, longer for bulk.
andrew: propose we escalate to high if vendor cannot prove deletion. For now keep medium.
sam: forensic checks: searched logs for `keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/ck-42` references — found 12 entries across envs: sandbox (9), staging (3). No prod refs.
andrew: that's good. still need to confirm there were no copies forwarded to external systems (queues, partner slack, etc.)
kai: I'll run a quick globs search across buckets: `gsutil ls -r gs://** | grep ck-42 || true` and return list — ETA 30m.
sam: PR to fix exporter filter: https://github.com/redwood/audit-exporter/pull/412 — adds whitelist of safe fields and drops metadata.key_wrap/key_id. Nina please review.
nina: reviewed, adding owners and will fast-track to hotfix pipeline. plan: merge, CI, and canary to sandbox, then backfill scrub for existing exports via script.
jules: scrub script idea: stream CSV through jq filter to drop metadata.key_* and rewrite copies with a quarantine tag. sample: `cat exported_events.csv | jq 'del(.metadata.key_wrap,.metadata.key_id)' > scrubbed.csv`
andrew: ensure we keep a forensic copy locked for 90 days under legal hold before scrubbing to preserve investigation evidence. legal: @legal-team hold requested.
legal-team: acknowledged. please add ticket LEG-INC-20241102-1 with list of artifacts.
nina: timeline recap:
- 10:26Z stopped exporter (kai)
- 10:40Z locked bucket access (sam)
- 11:00Z sam provides object list + redacted samples
- 11:45Z vendor attestation received
- 12:00Z nina to decide on KMS rekey vs rewrap after jules' assessment
- 12:30Z jules KMS impact assessment
- 14:00Z scrub/backfill job to run (subject to legal hold)
kai: logging change to pipeline to redact `metadata` subfields is in code review, will deploy after approval.
sam: anything else? we should also add alerting to detect future exporter serialization of key fields (CI unit test + policy gate).
andrew: created alert rule in monitoring: AlertID: SEC-AUDIT-METADATA-EXPOSE when export contains "key_id" or "key_wrap" fields — threshold 1 event.
jules: closing notes: this looks contained to sandbox/staging. recommend rewrap instead of full rekey unless vendor files persisted longer than attested.
nina: agreed. moving to action tracking in INC-20241102-1. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
